Abstract
This paper explores contradictions in Einstein's definition of simultaneity, and their contribution to the famous Twin Paradox. In the Galilean case, t = t', the Cosmonaut and Earth twins obviously age the same, but in the other cases we obtain ontological contradictions. The problem lies in Einstein's synthesis of non-motion and motion of one and the same light ray. Gauss's Modular or Time Arithmetic helps to identify and sort out the fundamental problems. Despite Einstein, only one time has ever existed: the present. The inequality of entities within the electromagnetic continuum creates the non-synchronicity we call motion.

Velimir Abramović argues that Einstein's definition of simultaneity is self-contradictory, that the contradiction is the source of the twin paradox, and that Gauss's modular arithmetic exposes it. The paper was given at the 18th Natural Philosophy Alliance conference in 2011.
He begins by quoting the 1905 paper in full on the point at issue: a common time for A and B cannot be defined "unless we establish by definition that the 'time' required by light to travel from A to B equals the 'time' it requires to travel from B to A," so that with a pulse leaving A at t A , reflecting at B at t B , and returning at t ′ A , the clocks are synchronised when
t B − t A = t ′ A − t B . (1)
Against this he sets "the constant present time of human experience where t A = t B ," and then works through the algebra. From (1) he obtains t = t B − t A and t ′ A − t A = 2 t , then forms differences that reduce to t A − t A = t ′ A − t ′ A = t − t , hence 0 = 0. Taking the other route, through t = t B − t A and t = t ′ A − t B , he adds them to get 2 t = t ′ A − t A , and again reaches 0 = 0.

title: Mathematicism and Atomism to Logical Etherism
content_preview:
Title Mathematicism and Atomism to Logical Etherism
Author(s) Jim Hodges
Keywords Atoms, Ether
Published 1997
Abstract
The paper explores the implications of the Margaret Wertheim dictum that physics is culturally determined and fallible. The followers of Pythagoras and Democritus have had a beneficial influence on the development of Western thought, culminating in Isaac Newton's law of gravitation/law of motion and John Dalton's atomic theory of matter. However the discovery of a solid elastic ether by Michael Faraday threw Newtonian mathematism and Daltonian atomism into crisis. The reaction of the Western scientific elite has been to bury the ether under a near impenetrable blanket of mathematical obfuscation. The first instance of this process occurred when Maxwell's ether based equations were de-etherized and mathematized by Heaviside and Hertz. A second and more serious instance was a reaction to Michelson's linear ether drift experiment and to Poincare's ether-Fitzgerald-contraction based impotence principle of relativity. This principle was de-etherized and mathematized by Einstein and Minkowski. However at the end of the 2nd millennium there is one small group who is especially able to transcend its cultural conditioning, i.e. the Natural Philosophy Alliance. From the papers of NPA members Ronald Hatch and F. Selleri it should be obvious that the physical universe is but a big blob of ether with vibrations in it.

title: Measurement of Gravitomagnetic and Acceleration Fields around Rotating Superconductors
content_preview:
Title Measurement of Gravitomagnetic and Acceleration Fields around Rotating Superconductors
Author(s) Martin Tajmar
Keywords Gravitomagnetic London Moment, Gravitomagnetism, Cosmological Constant
Published 2007
Volume AIP CP880
Abstract
It is well known that a rotating superconductor produces a magnetic field proportional to its angular velocity. The authors conjectured earlier, that in addition to this so-called London moment, also a large gravitomagnetic field should appear to explain an apparent mass increase of Niobium Cooper-pairs. A similar field is predicted from Einstein's general relativity theory and the presently observed amount of dark energy in the universe. An experimental facility was designed and built to measure small acceleration fields as well as gravitomagnetic fields in the vicinity of a fast rotating and accelerating superconductor in order to detect this so-called gravitomagnetic London moment. This paper summarizes the efforts and results that have been obtained so far. Measurements with Niobium superconductors indeed show first signs which appear to be within a factor of 2 of our theoretical prediction. Possible error sources as well as the experimental difficulties are reviewed and discussed. If the gravitomagnetic London moment indeed exists, acceleration fields could be produced in a laboratory environment.

Title Measurement of the Anisotropy in the Velocity of Guided Electromagnetic Waves
Author(s) Paul Ted Kolen
Keywords electromagnetic waves, Measurement, velocity
Published 1984
Abstract
In this thesis an experiment to detect anisotropies in the one-way velocity of guided electromagnetic waves and a theoretical model to interpret these anisotropies is presented. The experiment utilized the rotation of the earth to rotate the propagation path of a pulse train generated by a Cesium atomic clock via an environmentally controlled coaxial cable to a second Cesium clock. The second Cesium clock generates an identical pulse train and both are then compared at a time interval counter located near the second clock. Ideally, the difference in arrival times of the two corresponding pulses, one from each clock, represents the arbitrary initial synchronization of the two clocks and the one-way time of flight of the pulse generated by the first clock. Any variation in the time of flight is detected as a modulation superimposed on a constant offset in the differences of arrival times as measured by the time interval counter. In practice, along with the aforementioned offset and modulation, phase noise due to clock instabilities require that coherent summing techniques be used to increase the single day signal to phase noise (S/N) of 1/10 to an acceptable level. The sidereal coherent sum for 75 days of roundtrip data, taken simultaneously with the one-way, yields no coherent signal with a period equal to the fundamental summing period having an amplitude greater than 5 ps. title: Mechanical Dimensionalities of Electrodynamic and Gravidynamic Fields
content_preview:
Title Mechanical Dimensionalities of Electrodynamic and Gravidynamic Fields
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Jaroslav G Klyushin
Keywords fields, electric field, permittivity, density, Ether
Published 2010
Journal Proceedings of the NPA
Volume 7
No. of pages 3
Pages 257-259
Abstract
A system of mechanical dimensionalities is proposed for electrodynamics. It turns out that permittivity has the dimension of mass density. Therefore, the electric permittivity constant is interpreted as ether mass density. The vacuum magnetic permeability has dimension of compressibility, and it is therefore interpreted as free ether compressibility. The electric field has dimension of velocity. That enables us to compare its qualities with those of gravity, which has dimension of acceleration.
Overview
Mechanical Dimensionalities of Electrodynamic and Gravidynamic Fields is a three-page paper by Jaroslav G Klyushin of the University of Civil Aviation, St. Petersburg, presented at the 17th Natural Philosophy Alliance conference and published in Proceedings of the NPA volume 7 (2010), pages 257–259.
Its motivation is stated clearly and is a reasonable one. "A system of dimensionalities is actually the language in which we express our ideas in physics," and different branches use different languages, so that connections between them are obscured. Newtonian mechanics works in mass, metres and seconds; thermodynamics introduces temperature and heat as separate concepts; and electrodynamics is worse still, with several competing systems in circulation. Klyushin's aim is to express electrodynamic quantities in purely mechanical dimensions and thereby clarify the relations among electrodynamics, gravity and hydrodynamics.

Title Mechanical Image of Electromagnetism
Author(s) Giuseppe Cannata
Keywords Electromagnetism
Published 1989
Pages 33-52
Abstract
To attribute an inertia to free space is not an option. It is soundly consistent with the fundamental laws of physics. The mechanical interpretation of electromagnetic phenomena would supply a concrete way of simplicity and unification. Consequently the revised quantum theory could become without any contrast a modern chapter of a removated classis physics. Here is proposed a new elementary charge model, which simplifies the interpretation of many phenomena, including the controlled nuclear fusion. A reinterpretation of Maxwell's equations and a comprehensive demonstration of the value of the classical Planck quantum is given.

Abstract
The universe is neither empty nor void, but is instead filled with a single universal substance, the stellar air. Electromagnetic waves oscillate within the stellar air and can be visually described as constructs of the stellar air. Gamma rays are high frequency electromagnetic waves that compress the stellar air into quarks of liquid light at the resonant frequency of the stellar air within the Universe. title: Michelson-Morley Experiments Revisited and the Cosmic Background Radiation Preferred Frame
content_preview:
Title Michelson-Morley Experiments Revisited and the Cosmic Background Radiation Preferred Frame
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Reginald T Cahill
Keywords Michelson interferometer, Cosmic Background
Published 2003
Journal Apeiron
Volume 10
Number 2
No. of pages 14
Pages 104-117
Abstract
A new information-theoretic physics has given rise to a quantum-foam description of space relative to which absolute motion is meaningful and measurable. In this new physics Michelson interferometers operating in gas mode are capable of revealing absolute motion. We analyse the old results from gas-mode Michelson interferometer experiments which always showed small but significant effects. Analysis of the Illingworth (1927) experimental data, after correcting for the refractive index effect of the helium used, reveals an absolute speed of the Earth of v = 369 ± 123 km/s, while the Miller experiment (1933), after correcting for the refractive index effect of the air, now gives a speed of v = 335 ± 57 km/s, which are in agreement with the speed of v = 365 ± 18 km/s determined from the dipole fit, in 1991, to the NASA COBE satellite Cosmic Background Radiation (CBR) observations. The new physics also implies that vacuum interferometers will give null results, as has been observed many times. These experimental results imply that absolute motion is observable and that there is a preferred foliation of spacetime coinciding with the CBR frame.
Overview
Written with Kirsty Kitto at Flinders University and published in Apeiron in 2003, this paper makes a single, sharply drawn claim: that the classic Michelson–Morley -type interferometers were never null, that their small residual fringe shifts were mis-analysed because the light in them travelled through gas rather than vacuum, and that when the refractive index is properly accounted for the recovered speeds agree with the Earth's motion relative to the cosmic background radiation frame measured by COBE.

Microwave Power Measurements is a three-page article by Leslee A Kulba , published in 2010 in issue 48 of the Electric Spacecraft Journal , the journal's final double issue. It is the eighth part of the ten-part handbook on perpetual motion and its testing that Kulba, the journal's technical editor, contributed to that issue, and it is the most specialised of the ten.
The text of the article has not been recoverable, and this page describes its subject and its place in the series rather than its argument.
The subject
Why microwave power is a separate problem
At low frequencies, power is found by measuring a voltage and a current at a point. At microwave frequencies that stops working: the wavelength becomes comparable with the apparatus, voltage and current are no longer well defined along a line, and what can be measured instead is power flow — how much energy per second is travelling in each direction along a transmission line. Every technique below is a way of turning that flow into something a meter can read.
The subject earns its place in a handbook on energy claims because a good deal of the relevant experimental work — plasma devices, resonant cavities, and the microwave-driven arrangements in parts of the cold fusion and discharge literature — is done with radio-frequency and microwave excitation, and the input power is exactly the quantity a claim of excess output depends on.

Thermistor and bolometer sensors absorb the microwave power and detect the resulting change in resistance. title: Millennium Theory of Inertia and Gravity

Title Millennium Theory of Inertia and Gravity

Author(s) Joseph A Rybczyk
Keywords gravity, inertia, gravitation, Newton , Kepler
Published 2004

Abstract
Investigative analysis of Kepler's laws of planetary motion lead to the revelation that Newton's laws of mechanics are incomplete and improperly correlated with his universal law of gravitation. It is subsequently shown that even Galileo's discovery that all objects fall at the same rate is only conditionally true. Ironically, it is Newton's modification of Kepler's third law of planetary motion that provided the insights leading to these discoveries, including the required modification of Newton's universal law of gravitation. During the ensuing formalization process, Newton's laws of mechanics are expanded as required, and correctly incorporated into an expanded version of the universal law of gravitation. The newly interpreted, and properly correlated laws are concurrently and subsequently validated through mathematical analysis and found to be in full agreement with Kepler's laws, and consistent with Newton's, and Einstein's earlier determined fundamental principles of equivalence involving gravitational and inertial forces. The broad extent by which the physical, and astronomical, sciences are affected by this work gives evidence of the fundamental nature of the discoveries presented.

Journal of New Energy , Fall 2001 (Proc. Of the 2nd Int. Workshop: Physics as a Science , Galeczki, Marquardt, Wesley Eds.). The first purely mathematical and irrevocable proof of the incompatibility between "Minkowski space" and particle dynamics is presented. "Special" relativity was a tragic confusion between the independent Eulerian x ; y ; z ; t and Lagrangean x(t) ; y(t) ; z(t) coordinates of a particle moving under the influence of forces. Only continuous, field theories -like Maxwell' s-described by equations with partial derivatives could, if at all, be described by means of Eulerian coordinates. The dynamics of moving bodies, however, as discrete, atomistic theory, is compatible only with ordinary differential equations with the Lagrangean coordinates as solutions. In both types of theories non-invariant initial conditions are an indispensable part. Minkowski's expression (ct) 2 - x 2 is, therefore, not an invariant, since x -as-a-solution of an equation of motion contains the frame-dependent initial velocity. As "transformations leaving Minkowski's expression invariant", the Lorentz transformation loses is relevance for particle physics, too.

Abstract
The interpretation of some of theoretical foundations of physics will be changed. Planck's constant is known to be one of such foundations, which serves as a basis of quantum mechanics. Let us consider how a refinement of interpretation of the physical essence of this constant allows to make a theoretical penetration into the depth of electromagnetic structure of the electron and to connect this structure with the results of the experiment. Difficulties encountered in explaining the radiation of the theoretical black body were overcome in December 1900 when Max Planck supposed that energy, p E, in EM form is not emitted continuously, but discrete amounts Planck named quanta; that is: Ep = hn, where n - frequency of EM radiation; h - a universal constant later called Planck's constant.
Overview
Published in Apeiron in 2000, this paper by Philipp Kanarev of the Kuban State Agrarian University proposes a ring model of the electron , derived from a reinterpretation of what Planck's constant physically is.
Kanarev's starting point is that h does not have the dimensions of action in any illuminating sense but the dimensions of angular momentum, and that this has been under-exploited. He quotes the remark that "if Planck had determined his constant as a quantum of angular momentum modern physics would have been quite different." Combining E = h ν, E = mc ² and c = λν gives h = m λ²ν, and Kanarev observes that m λ² has the form of a moment of inertia. Adding the assumption that the radius of the rotating structure equals its wavelength, r = λ, turns this into h = mr ²ν — the angular momentum of a rotating ring.
From that he computes the electron's parameters: an energy of 5.11×10⁵ eV, a rotation frequency of 1.236×10²⁰ s

Abstract
The philosophy of structuralism asserts that science must use physical models in the quest to understand nature. According to structuralism and principles of the Judeo-Christian worldview, a proper and suitable model of matter must meet criteria of physical reality, truth, unity, and causality. Actual properties of the electron are compared to the properties of point-like models used in theories such as relativity theory, quantum mechanics, and the Dirac theory of the atom. "My Serious Challenge to Quantum Mechanics" is an article by Eric S Reiter published on 19 March 2019 on Beyond Mainstream .
Reiter reports beam-split tests with gamma rays that he holds contradict the assumption that energy is always both emitted and absorbed in quanta. His experiments, performed with both matter and light, indicate to him that conservation is preserved only if absorption is continuous and emission alone is quantised — which in turn implies a pre-loaded state in matter. Residence Murray, Kentucky, United States
Nationality American
Known for The earth battery; early wireless telephony
Nathan Beverly Stubblefield (22 November 1860 – 28 March 1928) was an American inventor and self-taught electrician of Murray, Kentucky, remembered for two things: a claim to priority in wireless voice transmission, and the earth battery that powered it.
The earth battery
Stubblefield's ground cell consisted of coils of wire buried in damp soil, drawing a continuous current from the electrolytic action of moisture and minerals in the earth. The claim that made it interesting to later researchers is that the output appeared disproportionate to any ordinary chemical action, and the device has been studied ever since by workers on unconventional energy, John Bedini among them. His coil is compared directly with the Rodin coil in work catalogued here: Rodin Coil vs Stubblefield Coil (2011 conference) and Rodin Coil vs Stubblefield Coil (2012 conference) .
Wireless telephony
Stubblefield began experimenting with wireless voice transmission around 1892 and gave public demonstrations in early 1902 of a battery-operated wireless telephone, portable enough to be used from boats. His early apparatus worked by conduction rather than radiation; the patent he eventually received in 1908 covered a wireless telephone system using magnetic induction . The patent was delayed in part because the trunk containing his apparatus was lost on a journey to Washington and he had to build another.
He died in poverty and obscurity in 1928. Murray State University holds a collection of his papers.

Neo-Newtonian Mechanics and Electromagnetism was a live session on 28 March 2026 in the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society live session series.
Application of Neo-Newtonian Mechanics to correcting and improving analysis of Electromagnetic Momentum and Electron Inertia in a Current Circuit. Presented by Dennis Allen and David M. Bower and hosted by Ian Cowan.
Summary
Dennis P Allen Jr and David M Bower presented the first of a planned series applying Allen's neo-Newtonian mechanics to electromagnetism. Allen supplied the theory; Bower took the slides, describing his own role as that of a graduate student learning the topic rather than an expert.
Variable inertial mass
The starting point is that inertial mass already varies with direction in relativity — a particle at relativistic speed accelerated along its motion gains mass by the gamma factor, one accelerated sideways by a different factor — a fact Allen said is not much dwelt on. He extends this: mass varies not only with velocity but with acceleration and with the jerk , the time derivative of acceleration. The mass change function depends on the magnitudes of both and on the angle between them, and a constant in it vanishes where there is left–right symmetry, so that the direction of a rotor's spin does not matter.
The motivation is the work of Alexander L Dmitriev in St Petersburg, whose horizontally spinning rotors show a small weight loss that falls to zero as the rotor slows. Dmitriev explains it by a gravitational induction analogous to Lenz's law. Allen's alternative is that the gravitational mass is unchanged while the inertial mass increases, so the upward inertial force pushes harder and the apparent weight falls. Abstract
A particle model of atomic hydrogen has been developed as a possible alternative to the currently ac-cepted quantum-mechanical approach. In the present work, the charged-particle motion within the model orbits are shown to generate magnetic and gravitational potentials that lead to the formation of spinning-disc, and thence to rotating-sphere hydrogen structures. The rotation of such structures occurs at the frequency of hydrogen's ground-state magnetic hyperfine transition, and accounts for atomic hydrogen's anomalous g-factor without requiring the intercession of electrons that spin perpetually in the absence of any driving force. Abstract

title: New Concepts for SpaceTime and Corroborating Evidence from Torsion Field Research
content_preview:
Title New Concepts for SpaceTime and Corroborating Evidence from Torsion Field Research
Read in full Link to paper (Internet Archive)
Author(s) Donald Reed
Keywords Torsion Fields
Published 1998
Journal Journal of New Energy
Volume 6
Number 1
Pages 22-24
Read the full paper here (archived copy — the original link is no longer available)
Abstract
A bold new theory has surfaced pertaining to the structure of microscopic nature which, in junction with the recent findings of Russian research on torsion fields, has potential astounding implication for not only clarifying our understanding of the operation of vacuum-energy devices, but might shed fresh insight into many of the counter-intuitive features of quantum theory, such as the aspect of non-locality which accompanies quantum "entanglement". The theory in question is the brain-child of physicist Mark Hadley, who has taken a truly maverick position, claiming that contrary to widespread belief, quantum theory is a consequence of the Einstein theory of gravity, instead of vice-versa. Expanding on the Wheeler-Misner theory of charged particles conceived as wormholes -- distortions in the topology of space -- Hadley has taken this approach one important step further. Positing sub-atomic particles as kinks in the topology of space and time, this new theory views elementary particles as a region of space-time so intensely warped that it bends back upon itself like a knot. Such a knot necessarily contains a "closed time-like curve". This time-loop, which is also one of the puzzling features of general relativity, enables a particle to interact with other particles not only in its past but in its future. Consequently, a new way of looking at entanglement is that sub-atomic particles, by virtue of the time machines they contain, are not constrained by time. There is nothing to prevent instantaneous interactions between particles, no matter the distance between them.
This article aka "Torsion Field Research".

Quantum theory is one of the most fascinating and successful constructs in the intellectual history of mankind. Nonetheless, the theory has very shaky philosophical foundations.
This book contains thoughtful discussions by eminent researchers of a spate of experimental techniques newly developed to test some of the stranger predictions of quantum physics. The advances considered include recent experiments in quantum optics, electron and ion interferometry, photon down conversion in nonlinear crystals, single trapped ions interacting with laser beams, atom-field coupling in micromaser cavities, quantum computation, quantum cryptography, decoherence and macroscopic quantum effects, the quantum state diffusion model, quantum gravity, the quantum mechanics of cosmology and quantum non-locality along with the continuing debate surrounding the interpretation of quantum mechanics.

title: Natural Philosophy Wiki
content_preview:
New Energy (also free energy , alternative energy or breakthrough energy ) is the umbrella term used in the dissident research community for work on energy sources that mainstream physics regards as impossible, unproven or already refuted. It is not a single theory. It is a loose federation of research programmes — cold fusion and low-energy nuclear reactions, the extraction of usable energy from the vacuum or zero-point field, "over-unity" motors and generators, and unconventional water, hydrogen and plasma processes — held together chiefly by the shared conviction that the accepted account of where energy comes from is incomplete.
Mainstream science's position is straightforward and should be stated accurately. Devices that deliver more energy than they consume are held to violate the first law of thermodynamics; the vacuum's zero-point energy is held to be a ground state, from which no net work can be extracted precisely because it is the lowest state available; and cold fusion is held to have failed the replication test in 1989 and to have earned its place as a standard example of pathological science. Two US Department of Energy reviews, in 1989 and 2004, declined to recommend a dedicated programme. Almost none of this work appears in the major physics journals, and most of it is funded privately or not at all.
The researchers documented on this wiki do not all agree with each other, and several of them are among the field's sharpest critics. What the literature collected here shows is a body of experimental and theoretical work — some careful, some not — that has continued for four decades outside the institutions, and the rest of this article sets out that work.
Related articles on this wiki: Cold Fusion , Energy , Aether , Dark Energy . The full paper index is at Category:New Energy .

Abstract
After twelve years of searching the world for new-energy devices that have a strong commercial potential, four have been identified. Four new-energy devices will be discussed. These four are:
High-density charge cluster technology which was first discovered by Kenneth Shoulders (USA) and later found by three other independent scientists.
Dr. Randell Mills discovery of collapsing the hydrogen atom below its ground state.
The Koldamasov device from Russia that vibrates a mix of light and heavy water through a special dielectric material to produce more thermal energy than used to power the oscillator.

New Energy News (NEN) was the newsletter of the Institute for New Energy (INE), a monthly (20–30 page) publication reporting on "new energy" and cold fusion research. It was founded and long edited, published, and funded by Hal Fox through the Emerging Energy Marketing Firm (EEMF) group in Salt Lake City; later Patrick G. Bailey took over as its contact, editor, and publisher.
History
Hal Fox published NEN as a printed, mailed newsletter until about 1999–2000, when it became an emailed newsletter. It ceased publication after May 2005. It is closely tied to the Journal of New Energy and the broader Institute for New Energy community.

Overview
This is Volume 8, Number 4 (April 2001) of New Energy News , the monthly newsletter of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Patrick G Bailey and distributed from Salt Lake City. It is not a research paper but a compiled issue — abstracts, a book review, reprinted news articles, an obituary, a long open letter, and a meetings calendar — and it is of interest chiefly as a snapshot of what the new-energy community was reading and arguing about at the turn of the century. The masthead of this issue announces a format change: from this point NEN would be circulated by email in both plain ASCII and PDF, with an Adobe Acrobat CD-ROM offered by post to subscribers who had no reader.
The issue's unifying theme is the vacuum. Its lead abstract is a mainstream Physical Review B paper on extracting work from the Casimir Effect ; its centrepiece is Tom Bearden's open letter to the National Science Foundation arguing that every existing power system is already drawing its energy from the vacuum without knowing it. Between these sit a Reuters report on the first negative-index metamaterial, a polemical book review, and a warning about global electromagnetic pollution. The editorial stance throughout is that a workable Free Energy technology exists or is close, and that its absence from the grid is a matter of institutional inertia and active suppression rather than physics.

Overview
This is volume 7, number 7 of New Energy News (ISSN 1075-0045), the monthly bulletin of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Patrick G Bailey and dated December 2000. It is not a research paper but a compilation: reprinted book and video reviews, a technical report contributed by a working researcher, the president's state-of-the-organisation message, forwarded newswire items on climate and nuclear power, and a substantial dossier of correspondence arising from a dispute with the American Physical Society's public-affairs office. The unifying theme across the issue is not a physical theory but a grievance about scientific gatekeeping — who gets to be heard, on what evidence, and through which institutions.

INE was then based at 3084 E. 3300 South, Salt Lake City, with annual membership at $35 including the newsletter, or $150 including four quarterly issues of the Journal of New Energy .
The issue's centre of gravity is the relationship between conventional energy policy and the "new-energy" field. Roughly half the pages are given over to a detailed digest of a U.S. Senate bill and a DARPA propulsion solicitation, the rest to short news items, a substantial book review, letters and meeting announcements. The editorial position running through the issue is explicit and repeated: that the commercialization of new-energy devices — cold fusion , zero point energy extraction, charge-cluster technology — would relieve strategic dependence on imported oil, reduce pollution, and improve economic conditions worldwide. That framing departs from the mainstream energy-policy literature of the period, which treated the renewable/efficiency portfolio as the whole of the alternative-energy question and did not admit the anomalous-energy claims as candidates at all.

It is a news bulletin rather than a research paper, organised into standing sections — Abstracts, Book Review, Articles, Letters and Meetings — and it announces the switch to distribution in both plain ASCII and PDF, with an Adobe Acrobat CD-ROM offered by post for $2 to readers without Internet access.
The issue is unusual in the New Energy News run for how much of it is given over to mainstream climate science. Roughly half the pages reprint the Shanghai draft Summary for Policymakers of the IPCC Third Assessment Report, together with BBC, Washington Post , New Scientist and Munich Re coverage of it. The remainder carries the newsletter's characteristic content: energy statistics, a critique of U.S. energy policy, a Hal Fox editorial on patent-office treatment of paradigm-shifting inventions, a cold-fusion patent defeat, and a call for papers for a Space Physics conference in India. The editorial through-line — stated most directly in Fox's piece — is that the institutions that certify what counts as a workable invention are structurally hostile to discoveries that fall outside the accepted model, and that this, rather than any failure of the evidence, is why new-energy technologies remain uncommercialised.

This is the January 2001 issue of New Energy News , the monthly newsletter of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Patrick G Bailey with material contributed by Hal Fox , Toby Grotz , Gary Vesperman , Win Lambertson , Eugene Mallove and others. It is not a research paper but a compilation: abstracts of recently published work, a book review, feature articles, reader correspondence, and conference announcements. Its organising sections are SHORT SUBJECTS, BOOK REVIEW, ARTICLES, LETTERS and MEETINGS.
The issue is dominated by one event — the California electricity crisis of the winter of 2000–2001 — and by the community's reading of it. Where the mainstream account attributed the rolling blackouts to deregulation, market manipulation and a decade without new generating capacity, the newsletter treats them as vindication: proof that conventional energy policy has failed and that the "new energy" devices its contributors have long advocated should be funded and commercialised immediately. That framing runs through the technical items, the letters and the editorial asides alike. Overview
This is the full July 2000 issue of New Energy News (vol. 7, no. 2, ISSN 1075-0045), the monthly newsletter of the Institute for New Energy (INE), edited by Hal Fox and published alongside the Journal of New Energy . Patrick G Bailey was INE president at the time. Overview
This is Volume 8, Number 7 of New Energy News (ISSN 1075-0045), the monthly bulletin of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Patrick G Bailey and distributed from Salt Lake City. The issue opens with a note that from this point the newsletter will be circulated by e-mail in two forms, plain ASCII and PDF, with readers lacking Adobe Acrobat invited to mail $2 for a CD-ROM — a small detail that dates the publication precisely to the moment when the cold fusion and free-energy community was migrating from paper and floppy disk to the web.
The issue is organised in five departments: Abstracts, Articles, Letters, Meetings and Advertisement. Its editorial character is that of a clearing house rather than a journal. Refereed abstracts from Fusion Technology sit alongside newspaper clippings, an unrefereed theoretical essay, a reader's letter describing a home-built antigravity experiment, and conference announcements from three continents. Nothing in the issue is peer reviewed by the newsletter itself, and Bailey's editorial interventions are limited to bracketed asides such as "[This is not energy related now, but it may be soon!]". The value of the document is therefore documentary: it is a snapshot of what the New Energy research community was reading, arguing about and organising in mid-2001.

Overview
This is not a paper. It is an issue of New Energy News — the newsletter of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Hal Fox and archived by Patrick G Bailey — and it consists almost entirely of a conference report. The subject is ICCF8, the Eighth International Conference on Cold Fusion, held at Lerici in Italy over four days in May 2000, with about 150 attendees, some thirty presentations and ninety poster papers.
The issue reproduces abstracts from the meeting with the editor's own comments appended to each, and opens with his overall impression. That impression is worth quoting in full, because it is more sceptical than the venue would lead one to expect:
"There is a lot of excellent scientific work being done to improve the various so-called cold fusion experiments … However, there is no PRESENTLY-PLANNED cold fusion device that is ready for commercialization. This editor's judgement is that the basic hydrogen-in-metals process is not sufficiently robust enough to become a major new-energy commercial success."
He then names the two technologies he does think have "strong commercial potential": Randell Mills's work at BlackLight Power, and the high-density charge cluster patents issued from 1992 onward, which he notes are "the first … in which the patents claim to be tapping space energy or zero-point energy".
The value of the document is as a primary source: it records, in detail and at the time, what the low-energy nuclear reaction field looked like at the turn of the century.

Overview
New Energy News (ISSN 1075-0045) was the monthly bulletin of the Institute for New Energy (INE), edited by Patrick Bailey and drawing heavily on material submitted by Hal Fox . This issue — volume 8, number 6, June 2001 — is twenty pages covering an editorial, abstracts, a book review, articles, letters, meeting announcements and an advertisement. It is a primary document of the Free Energy research community at a particular moment: mid-2001, with the California electricity crisis underway, and the newsletter itself transitioning to email distribution in ASCII and PDF.
What makes this issue worth reading is not a theoretical claim — it advances none — but its internal posture. Two of its longest items are attacks on free-energy fraud , printed without editorial defensiveness, alongside a technical letter challenging the measurement of the gravitational constant and an uncritical reprint of a UFO-disclosure document. That range within twenty pages is characteristic of the field's self-understanding at the time: the belief that the physics is genuine coexisting with an unusually blunt acknowledgement that most of what is sold under its name is not.
Editorial: mid-year insights
Patrick Bailey, INE president, opens with the California energy shortage, predicting rolling blackouts before October and hoping they will "attract more public attention to advanced energy conversion technologies." Overview
New Energy News was the monthly newsletter of the Institute for New Energy (INE), edited by Patrick G Bailey and distributed by email to members in both plain ASCII and PDF form. This issue — Volume 8, Number 3, ISSN 1075-0045 — is not a research paper but a compilation: a president's editorial, a policy piece by Hal Fox , forwarded news items, a book review, two speculative articles, correspondence and a meetings calendar. It is of interest chiefly as a primary document of how the new-energy community understood its own position in early 2001.
Two things give the issue its character. The first is the California electricity crisis, then at its height, which Bailey reads not as a shortage but as "a well-planned and executed business operation put into motion by a few people to make the most money in the shortest amount of time" — and, simultaneously, as the opening that would finally bring funding to alternative energy conversion research. The second is an insistence on measurement discipline that runs against the grain of the field: a substantial part of the editorial is devoted to explaining why many advertised over-unity devices are fraudulent, and how to tell.
Contents of the issue
President's Perspective: devices, fraud and funding
Bailey's editorial surveys the roughly 130 devices then listed in the INE database, ranked by both scientific and commercial interest, and sorts their status into seven categories. Most are still at the replication stage and "are not ready". Some "will probably never work" but are kept for reference. Some are known frauds. Some are under proprietary agreements; some have been placed under Secrecy Orders by military review boards within the U.S. Patent Office; and some are simply hidden, awaiting funding.

Overview
This is the May 2001 issue of New Energy News (Volume 8, Number 5, ISSN 1075-0045), the monthly newsletter of the Institute for New Energy (INE), edited by Patrick G Bailey and produced out of Hal Fox 's office in Salt Lake City. It is not a research paper but a movement document: a snapshot of what the New Energy community was reading, arguing about and organising around at the turn of the millennium. The issue runs to seven departments — Editorial, Abstracts, Book Review, Articles, Letters, Meetings and Humor — and opens with the announcement that the newsletter will henceforth be distributed by email in two formats, plain ASCII and PDF, with a mailed Acrobat CD-ROM available for two dollars to members without internet access.
For a reader of this wiki the interest of the issue lies in what it reveals about how a dissident research community sustained itself. There was no peer-review filter, no institutional host, and no journal willing to carry the work; instead there was a membership list of just over three hundred, a monthly deadline of the last Friday, a device database maintained by hand in an Excel matrix, and one annual conference. Bailey's editorial states the editorial policy in a single word and makes the reasoning explicit.
Contents of the issue
The President's Corner: an anti-editorial policy
Bailey, then INE President as well as NEN editor, devotes his editorial to how articles are submitted and what happens to them. Its first half is given over to the 2001 INE/EEMF Symposium held at the Quality Inn City Center in Salt Lake City on 26–27 October 2001: a welcome by Bailey and Hal Fox , the final programme, and a session-by-session summary of what was actually presented. Overview
This is the October–November 2000 double issue of New Energy News (Volume 7, Numbers 5–6, ISSN 1075-0045), the newsletter of the Institute for New Energy, edited by Patrick G Bailey with substantial contributions from Hal Fox . It is not a scientific paper but a compilation: conference reports, letters, book reviews, abstracts of experimental work, press clippings and commercial announcements, distributed by email in plain ASCII and, from this issue onward, also as a PDF. The editor's note opening the issue announces exactly that change, and offers to mail an Adobe Acrobat CD-ROM to subscribers who cannot download one.
Its value as a document is archival rather than argumentative. It captures the cold fusion and free-energy community at a specific moment — eleven years after the Fleischmann–Pons announcement, at the point where several strands (hydrino chemistry, charge clusters, transmutation, over-unity generators) were being promoted simultaneously to investors and to a sceptical scientific establishment. What makes the issue unusually interesting is that it does not present a unified front: the most substantial contributions in it are internal criticism, and the sharpest sceptic of the claims reported is a cold fusion advocate.

The issue opens with a letter from Donald Kelly of Space Energy Journal arguing that Randell Mills' BlackLight Power results deserve credence — two laboratories reporting output at multiples of input, a utility investing a million dollars — and that the U.S. Patent Office may be "in violation of their own Rules of Practice" in stonewalling five Mills patents. Overview

This October 2001 issue (Volume 8, Number 10; ISSN 1075-0045) runs to four departments — Articles, Letters, Meetings and Advertisements — and functions as the community's noticeboard rather than as a research paper. Overview
This is Volume 8, Number 9 of New Energy News , the monthly bulletin of the Institute for New Energy (INE), issued as "Special Symposium Issue Part II" for September 2001. It is a compilation rather than a research paper: seven items of varying length, most of them submitted by Hal Fox or Patrick G Bailey , reprinted or summarized from outside sources with editorial commentary attached. The subjects are missile-defence testing, a heat-resistant coating invented by an amateur, energy-policy advocacy, classified energy patents, a Russian claim of a new current source, wind power economics, and — at the greatest length — Bailey's own position paper on whether UFO and antigravity research belong within the INE's remit.
The unifying thread across the issue is institutional rather than technical. Every item is chosen to illustrate the same claim: that promising energy and materials work is being obstructed, either by credentialism inside professional science or by deliberate classification outside it. The issue contains no original experiment, no data and no derivation. Its interest to a reader of this wiki is documentary — it records what the new-energy community was arguing about in 2001, in that community's own words, and it includes an unusually frank statement by the INE's president about where he wanted the boundary of respectable inquiry drawn.

Publication history

Indexing

New Energy Technologies was a Russian magazine on unconventional energy, published in a parallel Russian and English edition by Faraday Lab Ltd of St Petersburg between 2001 and 2005 under the editorship of Alexander V Frolov . Its subjects were aether physics, experimental free-energy work, gravitation and antigravity, and what it termed space-time control. It ran to 23 issues.
The magazine is a useful record of Russian and post-Soviet work in these areas during a period when little of it was appearing in English, and its contributors were largely independent researchers and engineers rather than academics.
Holdings in the Aether Physics archive
An offline research archive assembled by John Reed and surveyed in September 2026 holds the magazine in two forms: 22 complete issues as PDFs, numbers 1 to 23 with number 20 absent, and 320 individual articles filed by issue, covering the same run. The documents are not hosted on this wiki.

Overview
This paper reports a home-built optical experiment and draws a large conclusion from it: that visible photons of one wavelength can transform into visible photons of another, and therefore that photons carry a small, variable "virtual rest mass" and do not all travel at exactly the same speed.
The experiment is disarmingly simple. Wagner displayed three thin vertical lines — green, yellow and red — on an LCD computer monitor against a grey background, and viewed them through a narrow bandpass filter that passes only yellow, in the range 562.5 to 587.5 nm. An LCD has only red, green and blue sub-pixels — there is no separate yellow channel — and the yellow line is produced by driving its red and green sub-pixels together at equal full intensity. Through the filter, the grey background and the red and green lines were almost entirely extinguished, but much of the yellow line remained visible .
Wagner's reading is that this is a direct demonstration of photon transformation: red and green photons were annihilated and genuine yellow-wavelength photons created in their place, since only yellow-wavelength light could have passed the filter. New Gaussian Electrodynamics (sometimes called Gaussian dynamics or simply Gaussian electrodynamics on this wiki) is a reformulation of classical electromagnetic theory developed from the 1950s by the MIT electrical engineer Parry Moon and the mathematician Domina Eberle Spencer , and carried on after Moon's death by Spencer with Philip J Mann , Uma Y Shama and others. It rebuilds electrodynamics on Ampère's original force law rather than the Grassmann–Lorentz force of the textbooks, and couples this to a universal-time account of the velocity of light in place of Einstein's relativity of simultaneity.
The name honours Carl Friedrich Gauss , who held that the fundamental problem of electrodynamics is to find the correct force between two relatively moving charges — the question the programme takes as its starting point.
The central claims
Ampère's force, not Grassmann's
In 1823 Ampère gave a law for the force between two current elements. In 1845 Grassmann gave a different one, the expression now known as the Lorentz force , and it is Grassmann's, not Ampère's, that entered the textbooks. The two are not equivalent: the Ampère force is a central force , directed along the line joining the two elements, and so obeys Newton's third law in its strong form between the elements; the Grassmann–Lorentz force does not, and for open circuits it yields a net force on an isolated system, which standard theory balances by assigning momentum to the field.

Overview
The volume gathers contributions on foundational problems in quantum physics and is associated with Krasnoholovets's program of submicroscopic quantum mechanics. In that framework, real physical space is treated as a tessellation of "primordial cells" (superparticles) — a "tessellattice" — and a particle is a local deformation of that lattice. Krasnoholovets also introduces "inertons," proposed elementary excitations that carry the inertial properties of moving matter. It is a companion volume to Developments in Quantum Physics .

Volodymyr V. Krasnoholovets is a Ukrainian physicist known for a deterministic, submicroscopic approach to quantum mechanics and gravity based on a cellular structure of space.

The book deals with the resurgence of nineteenth century electromagnetism in physics and electrical engineering. It describes a series of important experiments, and new technologies based on these experiments, which cannot be explained by and analyzed with the modern relativistic electrodynamics of the twentieth century. The Newtonian electrodynamics of Coulomb, Ampere, Neumann, and Kirchhoff, which was current from 1750 to 1900, is fully reviewed and greatly extended to deal with contemporary research on exploding wires, railguns and other electromagnetic accelerators, jet propulsion in liquid metals, arc plasma explosions, capillary fusion, and lightning phenomena. Much of the book is based on the atomic definition of the Amperian current element. Finite element techniques for solving many electrodynamic problems are described.

Many important and new observations that should be of equal interest to both the professional and the intelligent lay reader ... excellent book ... The application of some of these concepts developed by the authors can save many millions of dollars a year in electrical power costs in just the aluminum industry. There are and will be many other valuable commercial applications of the study of Newtonian Electrodynamics ... If you are seriously interested in cold fusion and new energy developments, or if you are an electrical engineer, a scientist, or a teacher of science, this book is a must-read for you. If you are an intelligent lay person or professional, you will find this book full of interesting insights into the history and practice of electrodynamics.

Newtonian Electrodynamics by David Bower was a live session on 14 October 2023 in the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society live session series.
David Bower reports on Dr. Peter Graneau & Dr. Neal Graneau's work in Newtonian Electrodynamics.
Summary
David M Bower 's survey of Newtonian electrodynamics, built around Peter and Neal Graneau 's book of that name. Ian J Cowan hosted. Ten minutes were lost to a camera and microphone failure at the start, and Bower's connection froze about forty minutes before the end and never recovered, so the discussion proceeded without him and he was unable to reply or to close. André K T Assis , whom Bower had invited, attended in the green room without speaking; Neal Graneau was invited and did not appear.
Bower set out his position on how he works: he tends to make things complicated before making them simple, the slides do not represent perfection, and — recalling advice from Harry Ricker to pick one topic and become the world's leading expert on it — he found that even one topic, this one, is overwhelming.
The force laws
His organising question is what "contemporary electromagnetic theory" actually consists of. Maxwell's four equations do not suffice, because they contain no force law; adding the Lorentz force gives what he proposed calling the augmented Maxwell equations, M +, and that is what the profession works with.
The Lorentz force law is, on his account, a version of Grassmann's law of 1845 with input from Biot–Savart — he showed the derivation, recasting Grassmann's expression in terms of a source and a test charge. This paper argues that the shift from Newton to Einstein in 1919 rested on mathematical errors, and that once those are corrected there was never any need to leave the Newtonian framework at all. Fields Electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, physics
Nikola Tesla (Serbian Cyrillic: Никола Тесла) (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American inventor, mechanical engineer and electrical engineer whose work established the alternating-current electrical system on which modern civilisation runs. He is equally important to this wiki for a second reason: throughout his life Tesla held to a mechanical, aether -based conception of space, matter and energy, and in his final decades he publicly and repeatedly rejected Albert Einstein 's theory of relativity and the notion of curved space. For that reason Tesla stands as the central historical figure for the free-energy, wireless-power and aether research communities documented here.
Biography
Tesla was born in Smiljan, in what is now Croatia, into a Serbian Orthodox family, studied engineering at the Polytechnic in Graz, and emigrated to the United States in 1884. In 1888 he patented the polyphase alternating-current induction motor and a complete system of AC generation and transmission – the basis of the electrical power system still in use today. He patented the resonant air-core transformer known as the Tesla coil in 1891 and demonstrated a radio-controlled boat in 1898. From 1899 his work turned to the wireless transmission of power, described below. He never managed his finances and died in poverty in New York on 7 January 1943.

In this type of motor a linear motion is imparted to one or more pistons by the compression and explosion of a combustible mixture of vaporized fuel and air. The energy released by the explosion is transmitted to a crank shaft which converts the reciprocating movement into rotation. With the passage of time the primitive device of the 1860s has evolved into a complex marvel of machinery capable of propelling an automobile at speeds in excess of 300 mph and yet it still bears the same basic configuration and the same mode of operation as that of its earliest ancestor.

Delightfil book for young readers. If you go to Goat Island at Niagara Falls, you will see a statue of Nikola Tesla inventor of the AC polyphase system, the electrical power system put in 100 years ago at Niagara Falls which is essentially unchanged today. I wrote this book to explain to young readers and adults alike Tesla's precise role in the development of this great invention. Before this invention, electrical energy could only be transported about one mile and then only for lighting homes. Afterwards, electricity could be transported hundreds of miles, and not just for lighting, but also for running household appliances and industrial machinery in factories. In addition, unlike the polluting coal operating electrical plants of that day, Tesla's invention was a clean energy creation using a renewable source of power. Before Tesla's creation, all major factories had to be located by rivers and powerful streams. Now they could be located everywhere. For these reasons, Tesla was honored by LIFE MAGAZINE by being listed as one of the 100 most important individuals of the last 1,000 years. Tesla received the Edison Medal in 1917, he was nominated for a Nobel Prize in the 1930's and he was further honored by the world when in 1956, the electrical unit the "tesla" was named after him. (MRI's measure in "tesla" units.) Thus he could stand beside such other electrical giants as Ampere, Watt and Volta. In this, the third book of the Tesla Presents Series, engineer-historian Leland Anderson provides the transcript of the 1902 U.S. Patent Interference investigation concerning Tesla's System of Signaling. The document, "Nikola Tesla vs. Reginald A. Fessenden," which is no longer on file at the U.S. Patent Office, contains Tesla's own depositions as well as those of his closest and most trusted associates, George Scherff and Fritz Lowenstein. Included is material on the history of radio-controlled devices, the first practical form of these being Tesla's radio-controlled "telautomaton" ? an operational boat first demonstrated to the public at Madison Square Garden in 1898. [1] In addition to describing Tesla's "individualization" techniques for obtaining secure noninterferable radio communications?the patent is today recognized as the fundamental AND logic gate, a critical element of every digital computer?the interference record also reveals that essential features of the spread-spectrum telecommunications techniques known as frequency-hopping and frequency-division multiplexing have their roots in the resulting patents. Furthermore, there are new disclosures by Tesla on the operation of his large high voltage radio-frequency oscillators at both the Houston Street laboratory and the Colorado experimental station. Rarely in the history of science do we encounter such opportunities to gain deep insight into the fundamental ideas and concepts of an esteemed scientist/inventor.

Nikola Tesla On His Work With Alternating Currents and Their Application to Wireless Telegraphy, Telephony, and Transmission of Power: An Extended Interview
Book

Nikola Tesla On His Work With Alternating Currents and Their Application to Wireless Telegraphy, Telephony, and Transmission of Power: An Extended Interview is the first volume of the Tesla Presents series, edited by Leland I Anderson and published by Twenty-First Century Books. It is not a book Tesla wrote. It is the transcript of a three-day interview he gave in 1916 to his own legal counsel, in preparation for expert testimony in the impending radio patent cases — an account never intended for publication, and therefore one of the least guarded technical statements he ever made.
Its value to researchers is as a primary source. Speaking to his lawyers rather than to the press or a lecture audience, Tesla traces his own work in sequence: from the first high-frequency alternators built at his Grand Street laboratory in New York and their associated tuned circuits, through the Colorado Springs experiments, to the Wardenclyffe plant at Shoreham, Long Island. The Tesla researcher James F Corum has described it as a "veritable Rosetta stone" for tracing the technical thought of one of the most distinguished engineering scientists.
Background
By 1916 the priority of Tesla's wireless work was a matter for the courts rather than the journals, and his counsel needed his account on the record. The interview was conducted as preparation for expert testimony, which shapes the document in two ways that matter to a reader.

While there exist many biographical popularizations about Nikola Tesla (several quite bazaar and sensationalized), to our knowledge no serious engineering analyses of his work have appeared since the benchmark studies of Bemard Behrend in the years preceding World War I. (Behrend, while an AIEE Vice-President, actively lobbied for the bestowal of the Edison Medal upon Tesla, the seventh of which was conferred upon Tesla in 1917.) For quite some time now, the authors have been involved with the analysis and experimental reproduction of the RF aspects of Tesla's work. A major portion of our effort has been to reexpress Tesla's turn-of-the-century physics into the engineering and analytical terms of today. In spite of the fact that his physical explanations often bear the mark of antiquated and faulty theory (he was laboring within the framework of nineteenth century physics), we have been overwhelmed by Tesla's intuitiveness, his careful power of observation, his uncanny experimental technique, and the accuracy of his published data. The man was a genius.
While there exist thorough, in depth, engineering studies of Tesla's polyphase AC power system and his induction motors, dating back to the investigations of Professor William A. Anthony (Chairman of the Department of Electrical Engineering at Cornell University) and Dr. Bernard A. To be sure, Nikola Tesla was a singular individual. In the 1930s the unorthodox inventor Nikola Tesla announced to the world a pair of novel inventions. The first was "teleforce," a particle-beam projector which Tesla intended to be used as an instrument of national defense. A year later, in 1935, Tesla claimed a method of transmitting mechanical energy with minimal loss over any terrestrial distance, providing a new means of communication and a technique for the location of subterranean mineral deposits. He called this system for mechanical power transmission "telegeodynamics." Here, these two important papers, hidden for more than 60 years, are presented for the first time. The underlying principles behind teleforce and telegeodynamics are fully addressed. In addition to copies of the original documents, typed on Tesla's official stationery, this work also includes two Reader's Aid sections providing guidance through the more technical aspects of each paper. The actual texts are followed by Commentary sections which provide historical background and functional explanations of the two devices. Significant newspaper articles and headline accounts are provided to document the first mention of these proposals. A large Appendix provides a wealth of related material and background information, followed by a Bibliography section and Index.

"No Negatives in Physical Electronic Circuits & Physics Itself" is an article by Bob de Hilster published on 8 October 2019 on Beyond Mainstream . It is marked by the author as work in progress.
Writing as an electrical engineer who spent a career designing circuit boards, de Hilster argues that there are no negative numbers in physics — only directions. A sine wave describing an electromagnetic wave takes negative values in half of each cycle, but nothing in the physical picture is negative: there is an up amplitude and a down amplitude, each with a magnitude. He develops the point through his Particle Model treatment of light.

Published 1995
Journal Galilean Electrodynamics

Abstract
The problem of how the movement of bodies affects electrodynamic phenomena is an open one in classical electrodynamics (as opposed to relativistic electrodyamics) because we cannot use the Lorentz covariance of Maxwell's equations in such context. We propose that this problem be solved through the concept of current and not via the notion of Galilean covariance or action-at-a-distance force laws of Weber's type. The resulting theory is shown to be consistent with all experiments to which it is applicable.

title: Non-Hertzian Waves May Involve Subquantum Particles

Title Non-Hertzian Waves May Involve Subquantum Particles
Read in full Link to paper (Internet Archive)
Author(s) Rochus Boerner
Keywords ether , longitudinal waves, scalar waves, Tesla , light
Published 1995
"Non-Hertzian Waves May Involve Subquantum Particles" is a short expository piece by Rochus Boerner on the question of whether longitudinal electromagnetic waves can exist in vacuum — the waves variously called "non-Hertzian", "longitudinal" or "scalar".
It is a summary rather than a research paper: about a thousand words, written for a general reader, with four references to the technical literature. It was hosted on the web page collection of Robert Neil Boyd at rialian.com, where the original has since disappeared; the text survives in the Internet Archive.
Read the full text here (archived copy) .
What it argues
Boerner sets out the case in four steps.
The nineteenth-century aether could carry two kinds of wave. If light is a mechanical oscillation in a medium, that medium should support both transverse waves, oscillating across the direction of travel, and longitudinal waves, oscillating along it — as water carries both surface waves and pressure waves, and at different speeds.
Only the transverse kind survived. Hertz demonstrated transverse electromagnetic waves experimentally, and those are the only ones mainstream physics deals with. Boerner is careful and correct about why: from the standard Maxwell equations "it can be mathematically proved that only transversal waves are possible in a vacuum." He is equally careful to note that longitudinal waves in a material medium — plasma waves in an ionised gas — are entirely orthodox.
Tesla claimed to have made the other kind. Tesla said he had generated longitudinal electromagnetic waves, and that they could not be shielded by a Faraday cage, travelled faster than light, did not fall off as the inverse square of distance, and could carry energy wirelessly. Abstract
By projecting that the stationary position defming the inertial background reference of the universe is a "dynamic occurrence" (rather than the "static condition" assumed by most theoretical physicists today), constantly being formed by an "active" nonlinear geometrical displacement of time with space, we are able to illustrate how the presence of mass causes a resistance to this "motion of time", thus creating a vicinity of "less active pressure density', resulting in an "implosive motion" of the inertial reference background at the location of the mass body. By utilizing the "Active Geometry" as described by this new "geometrodynamic" relationship of time with space, we find we are also able to exactly duplicate the mathematical results as obtained by the equations of Newtonian Classical Dynamics describing both the acceleration due to gravity at the surface of a body of mass and the distance an object will fall per unit of length of time in a gravitational field.
This now allows us to understand how still position in inertial background reference can move (or accelerate downward) with respect to still position in space, consequently revealing the actual mechanism responsible for creating gravitational force.

Its claim is stated compactly in the abstract: "in the standard Maxwell electrodynamics the class of gauge fields is much larger than it is usually stated." Kapuścik is explicit that he is not challenging Maxwell's equations — "We take it as the best theory for all electromagnetic phenomena" — but arguing that the usual potentials are only one choice among many.

title: Non-locality and Quantum Physics: The Part and the Whole
content_preview:
Title Non-locality and Quantum Physics: The Part and the Whole
Author(s) Gianfranco Spavieri
Keywords Non-locality, Quantum Physics
Published 1996
Pages 367-380
Abstract
Debates between reductionism and holism have flared, on and off, in the past decade. Following the mechanistic view of nature held by Newton and Descartes, physics has been highly reductionist in its attempt to explain phenomena by reducing them to simple terms. To reduce atoms and nuclei to their subnuclear components has been one of the guiding themes of theoretical and experimental physics in its search for the Urstoff, the basic essence of things. The limits of this approach have been pointed out by holistic thinkers who claim that organisms and natural systems must be considered as irreducible wholes. In the holistic approach, creativity and innovation are viewed as an intrinsic property of systems, the larger picture of systems containing fundamental aspects of the whole being lost through reduction. However, a global vision of modern physics shows that it does not really oppose holism, so that there is no reason why the tweo views cannot be reconciled within a rational framework. In order to provide elements which support this reconciliation, it is convenient to revise the polemical concept of non-locality and its relation with holism and with consciousness.
Presented at
Descartes and Scientific Thought (4 September 1996)

Abstract
Foundations of Electromagnetism
We prove that, when linearized, the governing equations of an incompressible elastic liquid yield Maxwell's equations as corollaries. The divergence of the deviator stress tensor is interpreted as the electric field, while the vorticity (the curl of velocity field) is interpreted as the magnetic field. title: Nonlinear Relativity and the Quantum Ether
content_preview:
Title Nonlinear Relativity and the Quantum Ether
Author(s) Friedwardt Winterberg
Keywords Nonlinear Relativit, Quantum Ether
Published 1985
Journal International Journal of Fusion Energy
Volume 3
Number 2
Pages 7-21
Abstract
This paper presents an heuristic procedure by which the Lorentz transformations follow from the interactions characterized by the quantum mechanical commutation rules. A nonlinear generalization of the Lorentz transformations is derived which departs from special relativity at very high energies and establishes the observable existence of a substratum (ether). This departure from the Lorentz' invariance yields a finite zero-point vacuum energy. In a limiting case, special relativity is recovered, but the zero-point energy diverges. The theory satisfies the principle that the space-time structure should be determined from interactions instead of being postulated a priori .

title: Nonlocality, Relativity, and Two Further Quantum Paradoxes
content_preview:
Title Nonlocality, Relativity, and Two Further Quantum Paradoxes
Author(s) Gino Tarozzi
Keywords relativity theory , quantum paradoxes, time and energy, nonlocality
Published 1997
Pages 149-160
Abstract
In his ongoing struggle against Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics, in several circumstances Einstein appealed to the principles of his relativity theory to prove either the inconsistency or the incompleteness of the standard point of view.
In the paradox proposed at the Solvay Congress of 1927, he showed that Born's probabilistic interpretation of the quantum mechanical wave function was unacceptable, since in the case of the reduction process, it implied the possibility of instantaneous actions at a distance, in contrast with one of the two postulates of special relativity. In the photon-box experiment of 1930, he stressed how, starting from the principle of equivalence between mass and energy, one was led to a violation of the indeterminacy relations between time and energy. In the famous paper written with Podolsky and Rosen in 1935, the celebrated EPR paradox or argument, he finally showed that the locality condition plus the reality criterion led to the incompleteness of quantum mechanics.

title: Nuclear Alternative: Redesigning Our Model of the Structure of Matter
content_preview:
Nuclear Alternative: Redesigning Our Model of the Structure of Matter
Book
Author William L. Stubbs
Published 2008
Publisher Xlibris, Philadelphia
Pages 146
ISBN 1436329272
Nuclear Alternative: Redesigning Our Model of the Structure of Matter is a 2008 book by the nuclear engineer William L. Stubbs . It is the full statement of his alpha-beta model of the atomic nucleus: the proposal that nucleons are built not from up and down quarks but from beta particles — electrons and positrons — and that nuclei hold together not by a strong force but by nucleons sharing those particles, in the way atoms share electrons in a covalent bond.
From that starting point the book builds models of more than 250 stable nuclei out of a small set of repeating modules, tabulates their masses against measurement in an appendix, and then uses the same models to give accounts of alpha decay, beta decay, fission and fusion that dispense with both the strong and the weak nuclear force. Stubbs had reached the central idea in 1993 while working as a reactor engineer; the book was written after he retired, and he presented its argument to the Natural Philosophy Alliance in 2010 as " The Alpha-Beta Model of the Atomic Nucleus ".
The publisher's description states its aim:
The Standard Model has been the model of choice for nuclear structure since the late 1960s. However, 40 years later, scientists are still struggling to validate it. Nuclear Alternative offers an alternative explanation for the structure of matter that uses particles and forces observed and characterized since the 1930s. By redesigning the models of the proton, neutron, and electron, and developing a nuclear binding mechanism similar to covalent bonds in atoms, the book systematically develops models for more than 250 stable nuclei. It then uses the models to explain alpha and beta decay, and nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.
— Publisher's description, Nuclear Alternative (2008)

title: Nuclear Reactor Theory and Design
content_preview:
Nuclear Reactor Theory and Design
Book
Author Roger A Rydin
Published 1977
Publisher University Publications
Pages 346
ISBN B0006WMH5I Invalid ISBN
There has not been a new or significantly revised textbook on Reactor Theory published for a number of years. In the meantime, computer codes have become more sophisticated and more universally available, and virtually every student has access to a computer. While a number of rather excellent older books exist, they usually contain at least one of two specific shortcomings. Either the books teach historic Reactor Theory, or they serve as compendia of knowledge for the advanced graduate student or researcher. The purpose of the present work is very simply to teach the beginning graduate or undergraduate nuclear engineering student, who may have little or no previous knowledge of the field, the basic principles and ideas of present-day reactor physics design. The approach taken here is oriented towards the understanding and use of computer methods, but the material is carefully arranged so as to give a reasonable analytic foundation for the solutions. The underlying physics and mathematics is continually emphasized.
Above all, the development of the ideas behind the methods is stressed. Where necessary, rigor has been sacrificed in order to present a detailed description of the essential underlying ideas. Advanced research areas are mentioned in many cases, but a conscious attempt has been made to keep the scope of the work confined to what material a first year graduate student should reasonably be expected to be exposed to in a single year. For many students, what is presented here is enough, because they will work in other areas of nuclear engineering. But for those who are interested in Reactor Theory as a career, this text should enable them to move to the advanced books and to tackle the literature.
The first three chapters are introductory in nature, and are intended primarily as reference material for self-study. F

For our expectations of an environment-safe planet, the outcome from the UN nuclear safety meeting in Vienna, 2011, is not a satisfactory solution. The proponents of nuclear power guarantee a safe future, but safety has been guaranteed also in the past. Furthermore, one main issue is avoided: the danger from the growing radioactive waste. The Fukushima disaster is the radioactive contamination that came from such waste. There is no recipe for cure for this man-made radioactivity, other than time spanning hundreds to thousands of years. The radioactive waste grows by 12,000 metric tons per year?a volume equivalent to 100 double-decker buses or a two-story building with a footprint the size of a basketball court. Book

Published 1997/1998
Publisher Infinite Energy Press

The announcement of cold fusion in March 1989 at the University of Utah was greeted with astonishment worldwide. Drs. Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons had claimed that an electrochemical cell with heavy water electrolyte and a palladium cathode gave rise to so much excess energy that the mysterious phenomenon had to be nuclear, and was probably a process related to nuclear fusion. Many scientists quickly took sides for or against cold fusion--mostly against. By the end of the summer the experts claimed cold fusion didn't exist. They said it was an experimental error and could not be reproduced. Actually, the story had barely begun. Provocative research had never ended. Cold fusion was and is very much alive. IN THIS BOOK, Dr. Mizuno describes both the dark and bright sides of the cold fusion story: the frustration, the boredom, the endless guerrilla war with scientists who wanted to stop the research, science journalists who appeared to thrive on the outpouring of supposedly negative results, fruitless battles to publish a paper or be heard at a physics conference, but then also the triumph of dramatic experimental results in the production of huge excess energy and the paradigm busting discovery of the low-energy transmutation of heavy elements found on cold fusion electrodes. It is impossible for one book to encompass the now expanding worldwide effort to understand the cold fusion enigma, but for those who want to learn about the rest of the story, this account of one scientist's experience on the frontiers of knowledge is an excellent beginning.

Abstract
No other manifestation of the earth has been as seemingly inexplicable as the earth's magnetic field. More than a thousand years ago, individuals in China set afloat in bowls of water tiny slivers of loadstone, the mineral now called magnetite, and discovered that the slivers quickly assumed a preferred direction. That observation led to the development of the magnetic compass, which is still used by navigators, hikers and others seeking a way to determine direction. William Gilbert's Die Magnete (1600), his definitive work, was based upon extensive magnetic measurements collected around the globe, which showed that the earth itself is like a giant magnet, rather than magnetism arising from an extraterrestrial source as supposed by others1. In 1838, the mathematical genius, Johann Carl Friedrich Gauss, proved that the earth's magnetism source is at, or very near, the centre of the earth2.
Overview
J. Marvin Herndon proposes that the geomagnetic field is generated not in the Earth's fluid iron–sulphur outer core but in a shell of fission products surrounding a natural nuclear reactor at the planet's centre, with the reactor supplying both the mechanism and the energy.
The paper is a short correspondence in Current Science summarising a programme Herndon began in 1979. Its foundation is that the Earth resembles an enstatite chondrite rather than an ordinary chondrite.
